titre: Capturing Emails With Quizzes: The Strategy That Actually Pays Off
description: Email returns $36 per $1 spent. But classic opt-ins barely convert anymore. The method that actually pays: the interactive quiz. Full guide for entrepreneurs.

blocs.html:
TL;DR:

Email is still the highest-ROI marketing channel for online businesses:

  • an average $36 return for every $1 spent (Litmus, State of Email Marketing 2024)

  • But classic opt-ins now convert just 2 to 3% of visitors (Sumo, GetResponse benchmarks).

  • Meanwhile, a well-built interactive quiz captures 30 to 40% of visitors as leads (Interact Quiz Builder benchmarks).

  • The quiz replaces the ebook. Here’s how to use it.

blocs.texte: Email Isn’t Dead. Far From It.

blocs.html:
Hey. If you’re running an online business, you’ve heard the line at least fifteen times: “Email is king.” And you’ve probably wondered whether that’s still true, or whether it’s just one of those marketing platitudes everyone keeps repeating out of habit.

Short answer: it’s still true. And it’s actually more true now than five years ago.

A Disruptive Advertising study showed email is 40x more effective than social media for acquiring new customers. The Litmus State of Email Marketing 2024 report confirms it: email returns an average of $36 for every $1 invested. And there are 4.48 billion active email users worldwide (Statista 2024) — more than Instagram and TikTok users combined.

Email is 40X more effective for acquiring new customers than social media

Why? Because it’s the only direct line you have to your prospects. No algorithm between you, no paywall. You write, you send, they read (or don’t, but at least they have the option).

Every person on your list is a real opportunity — someone who already showed interest in what you do. And as long as you don’t burn the relationship, you can talk to them for years.

There’s just one problem.

The classic capture methods (landing page + free ebook + basic funnel) don’t work like they used to. Your prospects have seen the playbook 200 times. They download your ebook, never read it, and forget you exist within a week.

The method replacing them: the interactive quiz. Stick with me, I’ll walk you through everything.

blocs.texte: What You’re Missing Without an Email Capture Strategy

blocs.html:
Before we talk about the solution, let’s look at what happens when you don’t have one. Spoiler: it’s less fun than it looks.

You Lose Your Visitors Into the Void

Without a capture strategy, here’s the typical scenario. Someone lands on your site, reads an article, looks at a sales page, and leaves. You don’t even know they came by.

That’s money evaporating every single day. Out of 1,000 visitors with no email capture, around 980 leave without giving you anything, and you’ll never get the chance to talk to them again.

Every visitor who leaves your site without subscribing is a potential prospect interested in your offer, evaporating into the digital void.

You Lose Control of Your Acquisition

Without an email list, you’re at the mercy of algorithms. Average organic reach for a business Instagram post is now around 4% (Hootsuite Social Media Trends 2024). Translation: out of 10,000 followers, your post reaches around 400 people on average. And it keeps dropping.

An email list is your only real marketing asset. No one can take it away. Not Meta, not Google, not Microsoft.

You Hit a Conversion Ceiling

Without a list, you’re selling to whom? People who randomly land on your sales page. Which means not many — and definitely not qualified.

With a list, you can nurture the relationship over 3, 6, 12 months before the prospect buys. Most online sales happen after multiple touchpoints, not on the first hit. For context: average email open rate sits around 21.5% across industries (Mailchimp Email Marketing Benchmarks 2024) — meaning every send reaches roughly 1 in 5 of your subscribers. No social network comes close to that ratio.

Anyway, you get the picture.

blocs.texte: The Real Benefits of a Solid Capture Strategy

blocs.html:
OK, now that we’ve covered what kills businesses without an email strategy, let’s look at what changes when you actually have one.

You Build an Audience That’s Yours

Your Instagram followers belong to Meta. Your TikTok followers belong to ByteDance. Your LinkedIn connections belong to Microsoft.

Your email subscribers belong to you.

You can export your list, migrate it to another tool, use it for custom audiences in ads, run surveys with it. It’s your most valuable business asset, period.

You Sell When You Want

Launching a new offer? You email your list. Limited-time promo? Email. Webinar? Email. Product update? Email.

No waiting for your post to break out of the Instagram feed. No paying Meta to reach 5% of your own audience. You write, you send, it’s in their inbox.

You Nurture the Relationship Long-Term

A good email sequence is six months to a year of automated communication with a prospect. It gives them time to get used to you, your style, your ideas. The day they’re ready to buy, they already know who they’re dealing with.

That’s what marketers call nurturing. And it’s a thousand times more effective than throwing a sales page at cold traffic.

blocs.texte: How to Capture Emails Effectively (The Real Method)

blocs.html: Now we get concrete. You know WHY you need to capture emails. Here’s HOW to do it well.

1. A CTA That Hits Hard

First thing: your CTA. The button, the headline, the explicit invitation to drop their email. If it’s weak, no one clicks.

CTAs that actually work: - “Find out your profile in 2 minutes” - “Get your personalized diagnosis” - “What kind of [your avatar] are you?”

Avoid at all costs: - “Sign up for my newsletter” - “Stay in the loop” - “Get our updates”

Too generic. Too dated. Your prospects know that means mass communication with no real value.

2. An Irresistible Offer

Why should your visitor hand over their email? What do you give them in exchange?

The free ebook isn’t enough anymore. What works:

  • A personalized diagnosis based on their profile

  • An interactive mini-course

  • Access to an exclusive resource

  • A personalized promo code

And what works best: an interactive quiz that combines several of these at once.

3. An Interactive Quiz That Qualifies

Here’s the actual cherry on top, and the reason I’m writing this article.

A quiz is a fun, engaging mechanism that does three things at once:

  • It captures the email — the visitor plays a game, naturally agrees to drop their email to see results

  • It qualifies your prospect — their answers tell you their profile, level, real needs

  • It pre-sells your offer — the results page can route them to an offer matching their profile

Interact and Outgrow benchmarks across hundreds of published quizzes show an average capture rate of 30 to 40% of visitors, vs 2 to 3% for a classic opt-in. That’s 10 to 15x more leads for the same traffic, without spending more on ads. And with a tool that handles everything for you (more on that below), setup takes an afternoon.

blocs.texte: Case Studies: Brands Crushing It With Quizzes

blocs.html: A few concrete examples to show the method works.

Airbnb Tripmatcher

Airbnb runs a quiz called Tripmatcher that helps visitors discover their “traveler personality.” At the end, the visitor enters their email to see results and get destination recommendations matching their profile.

Devilishly effective. The visitor spends 4 to 5 minutes engaged with the brand, shares their profile, and walks away qualified. Airbnb now knows exactly which types of trips to push them in future campaigns.

Eric Bandholz built Beardbrand from scratch using a single Typeform quiz: "What type of beardsman are you?". Result: 150,000+ leads captured straight into the email list. But here's the twist — the quiz answers also became Beardbrand's best market research tool. When Eric saw most respondents traveled often, the brand launched a travel-friendly product line under 100ml. One quiz, two wins: leads captured AND the product roadmap informed by real customer signals.

That's exactly the kind of multi-purpose mechanic we talked about earlier: a well-built quiz captures emails, qualifies your audience, AND tells you what to sell next.
